chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from his father, from one of his men, who said:

A man came to Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have been deprived of night prayer.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'You are a man whose sins have restricted you.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why am I unable to perform night prayer according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) diagnoses the man's inability to perform *Qiyam al-Layl* not as a lack of time or energy, but as a spiritual consequence of his sins, which act as a 'chain' or restraint. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the reciprocal relationship between worship and sin: just as sins create barriers to divine grace, consistent prayer helps break these chains. The Imam’s response serves as both a diagnosis of spiritual stagnation and an implicit invitation to repentance to restore the capacity for devotion.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Imran Bin Musa, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali Bin Al-Numan, from his father, from one of his men who said,

‘A man came over to Amir Al-Momineen Aliasws Bin Abu Talibasws, so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I have been deprived of the Salāt at night’. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘You are a man, your sins have restricted you’.
en.sarwar: 34. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Imran ibn Musa from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from his father from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“A man came to Amir al-Mu’minin Ali, ibn abu Talib, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ’O Amir al- Mu’minin, I am deprived of Salah (prayer) at night.’ Amir al-Mu’minin said, ‘Your sins have tied you down.’”
